title: Phayao to Nan Road Trip: 3 Days 2 Nights Northern Thailand | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A cross-province Phayao-Nan road trip in northern Thailand: start at Kwan Phayao lake, drive the mountain road through Dok Khamtai, Pong and Chiang Muan into Nan, see Wat Phumin, then push on to Pua and Bo Kluea. Laid out day by day.
keywords: Phayao to Nan road trip, Phayao Nan itinerary, things to do in Nan, Kwan Phayao, Wat Phumin, Bo Kluea salt wells
h1:
Phayao to Nan, 3 Days 2 Nights
A Quiet Northern Mountain Route
intro: Phayao and Nan sit right next to each other, yet most people drive straight past Phayao on the way to Nan without stopping — even though linking the two is easy. This trip starts at Kwan Phayao lake in the morning, then takes the mountain road through Dok Khamtai, Pong and Chiang Muan, crossing into Nan province at Ban Luang before wrapping up in Nan town and the Pua-Bo Kluea area. It's a route most travellers haven't covered yet: good views, light traffic, and a slow pace that suits anyone who likes to take their time.

blocks.html: The popular way to drive from Phayao to Nan runs through the districts of Dok Khamtai, Pong and Chiang Muan, crossing into Nan province at Ban Luang before dropping down into Nan town (using Highway 1091, then stretches of 1148/1251). It's roughly 140–160 kilometres, but on a winding mountain road, so plan on about 3–4 hours of actual driving if you don't stop. The upside is light traffic and open ridge-line views in places. The thing to watch is that some sections have lots of curves and phone signal drops out, so fill the tank up before leaving Phayao and you'll have one less thing to worry about.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: This route is best if you drive yourself or rent a car — there's no direct public transport along it. Without your own car you'd have to take a bus the long way around through Phrae, which is much further. Aim to leave Phayao in the late morning and avoid driving the mountain road after dark, since there's very little road lighting.

blocks.text: The full route at a glance

items: Day 1 — Morning at Kwan Phayao lake and the temples, then the mountain drive into Nan town. Overnight in Nan.
Day 2 — Explore Nan's old town: Wat Phumin, cafes, the walking street. Second night in Nan.
Day 3 — Drive up to Pua and Bo Kluea, take in the rice fields and the Road No. 3 viewpoint, then loop back.

blocks.html: If you only have 2 days, drop Day 3 and use the afternoon of Day 2 to see more of Nan town instead. If you have more time, it's easy to spend an extra night at Pua or Bo Kluea — that area has plenty of homestays out among the rice fields to choose from.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Kwan Phayao, then over the mountains into Nan

items.activity: Kwan Phayao in the morning
items.note: The largest freshwater lake in northern Thailand. Early mornings are cool and pleasant — walk along the shore or grab a coffee and watch the sunrise reflect off the water.

items.activity: Boat out to Wat Tilok Aram
items.note: A 500-year-old temple in the middle of the lake that you reach by boat. The ride is around 20 THB per person, and it's a spot the locals here are proud of.

items.activity: Wat Si Khom Kham
items.note: A large temple by the lake, home to the great Phra Chao Ton Luang Buddha in Lanna style. It's right on the main road in and out of town, so it's an easy stop for a quick visit before leaving.

items.activity: Hit the mountain road
items.note: Drive through Dok Khamtai heading toward Pong and Chiang Muan. This is where the climbing starts, so top up the tank at a large station before heading deeper into the hills.

items.activity: Lunch stop at Chiang Muan / Pong
items.note: These district towns have rice-and-curry shops and local noodle places. It's your last proper rest stop before crossing into Nan — after this, places to eat get few and far between.

items.activity: Cross into Nan province at Ban Luang
items.note: The ridge section opens up with nice views and pull-offs for photos here and there. Drive slowly — there are lots of curves and phone signal cuts out in stretches.

items.activity: Arrive in Nan, check in
items.note: Pick a place to stay near the town centre, close to Wat Phumin, so it's easy to walk around. Save some energy for an evening stroll.

items.activity: Evening walk through Nan old town
items.note: As it cools off, wander around Wat Phumin and Wat Ming Muang, take some shots in the evening light, and find a local restaurant for dinner.

blocks.title: Where to eat dinner in Nan
blocks.html: Nan town has several local restaurants. Huean Hom, for instance, is known for nam ngiao (a northern noodle soup), khanom jeen and other northern dishes, set in a wooden house. If you're after miang pla khang — fresh Nan River fish — you can find that in town too.

items.activity: Khao soi breakfast beside Wat Phumin
items.note: Khao Soi Ton Nam sits near Wat Phumin in a two-storey wooden house, open from morning into the afternoon. They also do nam ngiao and boat noodles, and the place has been part of the town for ages.

items.activity: Wat Phumin
items.note: Nan's signature temple, with the only cruciform ordination hall of its kind in Thailand. Inside are the Pu Man Ya Man murals — the 'whispering lovers' painting people come specifically to see.

items.activity: Nan National Museum + the frangipani arch
items.note: An easy walk from Wat Phumin. Photograph the tunnel of frangipani trees in front of the museum — it's one of the town's classic photo spots.

items.activity: Wat Phra That Chang Kham + Wat Ming Muang
items.note: Keep temple-hopping around the old town — these are all within walking distance of each other, a cluster of old temples close together.

items.activity: Lunch break
items.note: Pick a northern restaurant in town, or the cafe behind Wat Phumin that does khao soi, nam ngiao and has good photo corners.

items.activity: Afternoon at a cafe
items.note: Nan has plenty of wooden-house cafes and cafes with rice-field views. Duck out of the afternoon heat, sip a coffee and rest your legs before round two.

items.activity: Wat Phra That Khao Noi for the view
items.note: A short drive up a low hill near town — a high vantage point over Nan at sunset, where you can see the whole town spread out below.

items.activity: Kad Khuang Mueang Nan walking street
items.note: Open only on Fridays and Saturdays, near Wat Phumin. There's local food, khantoke meals, and handmade craft souvenirs — don't miss it if your dates line up.

blocks.html: Nan's walking street only runs on Friday and Saturday nights. If your trip doesn't fall on those days, just use the evening to wander the old town instead — the area is pleasant to walk and the shops stay open into the evening anyway.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Up to Pua and Bo Kluea for the rice fields

items.activity: Leave Nan town heading for Pua
items.note: Take Highway 1080 north, around 60 kilometres. The road is better than yesterday's route into Nan, with rice fields and mountains on both sides.

items.activity: Cafe among the rice fields in Pua
items.note: The Pua area has several cafes with rice-field views, like the ones over near the Tai Lue village. Sit with a coffee and look out over the green paddies (or golden ones late in the rainy season) — it's the shot people come for.

items.activity: Wat Phuket and the terraced fields
items.note: In Pua, the temple grounds open out onto rice fields with the Doi Phu Kha range as a backdrop — one of the most popular viewpoints in this zone.

items.activity: Drive up to Bo Kluea via Road No. 3
items.note: This stretch is a scenic mountain road, with the Road No. 3 viewpoint and switchback curves worth stopping for. Take it slow and enjoy the drive.

items.activity: Bo Kluea ancient salt wells
items.note: Mountain salt wells where villagers have boiled salt the traditional way for generations. Watch how it's done and pick up some salt or salt soap as a souvenir.

items.activity: Decide: stay on or head back
items.note: If you have time, drive on to Sapan and spend a night in the valley. If time's tight, start the drive back to Nan town before dark to avoid the mountain road at night.

blocks.title: About drive times
blocks.html: The Pua-Bo Kluea-Sapan zone is all mountain roads — distances look short but take longer to drive than you'd expect. Build in plenty of buffer and don't pack the day too tightly, so you can travel at an easy pace without rushing.

items.name: Stay in Nan town (recommended)
items.blurb: Accommodation in the old town near Wat Phumin, within walking distance of the cafes and the walking street. It's the most convenient base for this trip.

items.name: Stay in Pua or Bo Kluea
items.blurb: Homestays out among the rice fields and along the streams, perfect if you want to wake up to morning mist and mountain views. Add a night here if you have time.

items.name: A night in Phayao before you start
items.blurb: If you're coming from the south, spend a night in Phayao first so you can start Day 1 at Kwan Phayao in the morning without rushing.

blocks.text: When is the best time to go

blocks.html: The cool season (November–February) is best — cool air, clear skies and sharp mountain views. It's the favourite time to head up to Bo Kluea and Sapan for the morning mist. Late in the rainy season (September–October) the rice fields are an intense green and gorgeous, but the mountain roads can be slick and the fog thick, so drive carefully. The hot season is the quietest of all, but the views look drier.

items: Cool season — sharp views and beautiful morning mist, but the busiest; book accommodation ahead.
Late rainy season — green paddies, but slick mountain roads; mind the curves.
Hot season — fewer people and cheaper rooms, but the photos may not be as green.

faq.q: How long does it take to drive from Phayao to Nan?
faq.a: The route through Dok Khamtai, Pong, Chiang Muan and Ban Luang is roughly 140–160 kilometres on a winding mountain road, so plan on about 3–4 hours of actual driving if you don't stop. Allow extra time and leave in the late morning — don't drive this road after dark, as there's very little lighting.

faq.q: Can I do this route without driving myself?
faq.a: There's no direct public transport along the Phayao-Nan route. Without your own car you'd have to take a bus the long way around through Phrae, which is much further. This trip is better suited to driving yourself or renting a car — you'll be more flexible and able to stop at the viewpoints along the way.

faq.q: How many nights, and where should I stay?
faq.a: The standard plan is two nights in Nan town, using it as a base to explore the old town and head up to Pua and Bo Kluea. If you want to take Bo Kluea and Sapan at a relaxed pace, add one more night in that area. For Phayao, a morning stop on Day 1 is enough.

faq.q: Are there restaurants and petrol stations along the way?
faq.a: Yes, in the district towns of Dok Khamtai, Pong and Chiang Muan. Once you head deeper into the hills around Ban Luang, shops and stations get further apart. Fill the tank up and have lunch in Chiang Muan or Pong before crossing the mountains.

faq.q: Who is this trip best for?
faq.a: It suits anyone who likes to travel slowly, drive for the scenery, and enjoys old temples, lakes and mountain rice fields. It's a route most travellers haven't covered yet, with light traffic. It's less suited to people who want big-city comfort and convenience, since many stretches are mountain road with no phone signal.
